input.body:
The `claude-code-web-users-support` pack changes shape in missingbulb/Claudinite#2189: each person owns a **pack directory** in this store rather than one Markdown file, and it is copied into a member's session pack root where that member's own engine loads it like any other pack. A person is no longer limited to prose; the same directory can carry skills, checks and a provenance log.

This moves the one file that exists, `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL].md` to `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL]/RULES.md`, and rewrites the store's README for the new shape.

**Merge order.** The reader opens the directory and nothing else, with no tolerance for the old address, so this and missingbulb/Claudinite#2189 are a pair. Merging this one first leaves personal rules unloaded until the pack change lands and members converge, which is the agreed interim rather than a regression to avoid.

The README also now says plainly what the shape implies: write access under someone's directory is the power to run code in their sessions, because a pack's checks and skills execute inside every session it is copied into.

The personal-pack change (#2189) reshaped `claude-code-web-users-support` around a pack directory per person. One name survives it for consumers only.

`provenanceDirOf` in `packs/claude-code-web-users-support/worldRules/preferences-provenance.mjs` returns `<path>-provenance`, the sidecar folder a person's provenance sat in while the store was flat. No layout has that folder any more and nothing in this repository calls the function. It stays because a member's own local pack may have imported it, and the pack and engine lanes deliver on separate cadences.

## What this issue removes

- `provenanceDirOf` and its `@legacy-tolerance` marker.

## When

One convergence window after #2189 merges, which is what puts the new pack in front of every member. There is nothing to census here: the function is this repository's own, so the condition is the window passing rather than any member's state.

Previously this issue tracked the tolerance for the retired `<email>.md` address. That tolerance was never shipped: the owner chose to convert the one store that exists (missingbulb/Shepherd#698) instead of carrying a second address, so #2189 removes the address outright and a member that has not taken it loads nobody's rules until it does.

---

input.body:
The `claude-code-web-users-support` store held one `<email>.md` per person, so the only thing a person could carry into a session was prose. Each person now owns a **pack directory** in the store, copied into a session-only pack root that the engine loads like any other.

Pairs with missingbulb/Shepherd#698, which converts the one store that exists.

## The shape

`<path>/<email>/` in the store is an ordinary pack directory: `RULES.md`, an optional `pack.mjs`, `skills/`, `worldRules/`, `declared-checks.json`, `provenance/`. At session start it is copied into `.claudinite/temp/packs/current_user/`, and from there the existing loader does the rest: rules on the memory channel through the generated index, skills mounted, checks run.

Two modules do it, each named for its job. [`copy_user_pack_to_repo.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/bold-planck-1nx6ru/packs/claude-code-web-users-support/copy_user_pack_to_repo.mjs) copies the directory in. [`user_pack_address.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/bold-planck-1nx6ru/packs/claude-code-web-users-support/user_pack_address.mjs) says where that directory is and whether this session may go and get it.

**The engine gains two things.** A third pack root beside the canon and the repo's own local packs, active by presence rather than declaration (nothing about a person is the repository's to declare) and **opt-in per reader**, so a shelf conformance sweep, a vendoring pass or a catalog generator is answered as if the directory were not there. And a `session-prepare` phase on the existing step runner, running before anything reads the session's pack set, whose stdout the orchestrator redirects away from session context.

**The index carries a literal line.** A generator running at converge time cannot discover a directory a session writes hours later, so the import is spelled out, and appears only where a declared pack ships a prepare step. The runner guarantees the file exists, empty when nobody's pack is there, so the import never dangles.

**No status file.** The copied directory is the whole interface. Its placeholder says nothing landed, and why is a pure function of the config and the environment, which `declineReason` answers once for the step that stops and the step that explains.

## Reaching the store

Local-first when this repo *is* the store, otherwise a shallow, blob-filtered, sparse `git clone` of the one directory. The GitHub tree API 403s behind the sandbox proxy and this repo's own guard records codeload as commonly denied where git against the same repository is not. Verified against the real store: the live copy from `missingbulb/Shepherd` found the owner's file and reported it.

## Compatibility

**No tolerance for the retired `<email>.md`.** Converting the one store that exists is cheaper than carrying a second address forever, so a member that has not taken this version loads nobody's rules until it does. That interim is agreed, not an oversight.

`consumer-safe-change` asked which of its three answers the removed exports take. **A deprecated alias**, not a migration record and not a fixture: `provenanceDirOf` stays where it was and #2188 removes it one convergence window out. A record would move the fleet for a rename nothing here requires, and a fixture would only prove the canon's own packs still converge. `store.mjs` itself is deleted with no shim: it was a six-day-old internal module of a pack nobody extends, and the check that speaks for members here is silent on it.

The two engine exports this pack newly reads come through a namespace import with a capability guard, because the lanes deliver separately and a named import of an export a member's engine lacks is a link-time error that faults the whole pack.

**Two rules were deliberately reworded**, which `rules-append-only` reports as removals: `person-asking-change` and `person-asking-record` keep their ids and their strength, and now name a directory where they named a file. Both carry the entry on their provenance file.

## Folders touched

```
engine/pack_loader/    the third pack root and its opt-in, the prepare phase, the
                       index's literal line, the summary's exclusion of copied packs
engine/hooks/          the orchestrator runs the prepare phase first with its stdout
                       kept out of session context; the session readers opt in
packs/claude-code-web-users-support/
                       the two renamed modules, the two steps that call them, and the
                       store checks, which judge directories and in-pack provenance
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/
                       the member-side index rule exempts the one import no checkout
                       can satisfy
engine-tests/, packs/*/test/
                       coverage for each of the above
```

## What was verified

- Whole suite green: 3795 tests, 0 failures.
- `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both exit 0, with no blocking findings.
- The copy, both engine paths and the missing-pack case run end to end against a real git store.
- See-it-fail confirmed for the copied-pack reset, the index's literal line and the summary's exclusion.

Found along the way, and fixed here: importing the step runner for one constant ran its program and killed the importing process, and `path.relative` on two relative paths reaches for `process.cwd()` at import time, which faults in a process whose cwd was deleted.

Refs #2188

content.text:
You were right on all three counts. Done, pushed, and the store is converted.

## `store.mjs`, and why it is now `user_pack_address.mjs`

It answered two questions and its name announced neither. The first is **where** a person's pack lives: it reads this pack's entry config, validates that `repo` looks like `owner/name` and that `path` does not escape upward, and returns `{ repo, path }` or null. Null deliberately collapses "nothing declared" with "declared but broken", because every caller's next move is the same and one check reports the difference. It also turns a store plus an identity into the repo-relative directory, and refuses an identity that would not be safe as a path segment.

The second is **whether this session may go and get it**, which is new. That list of reasons used to live inside the copy step; it is now `declineReason`, a pure function of the config and the environment, shared by the step that stops and the step that explains. One list, so a session can never be told a reason that is not the one that fired.

The file is `store.mjs` no longer because "store" named the shape the data sits in rather than what the module gives you. It gives you an address and a permission.

## The receipt

You were right that it was not needed, and your reasoning is the one I should have applied. The directory already is the answer. It holds either the person's pack or a placeholder, and the placeholder plus `declineReason` reconstructs everything the receipt carried, with no file to keep in step. I had reached for it because two steps needed to agree, and I solved that with state instead of with a pure function.

One thing did survive the deletion. The reporting step still needs to tell "nothing landed" from "here are your rules", and it does that by comparing the prose file against the exported placeholder text.

## The single file

Gone entirely, with no tolerance. [Shepherd PR #698](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/pull/698) moves `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL].md` to `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL]/RULES.md` and rewrites the store README for the directory shape, including the sentence that write access there is the power to run code in someone's sessions. [Issue #2188](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2188) no longer tracks that tolerance; it now tracks the single deprecated alias the conformance check insisted on.

```
packs/claude-code-web-users-support/   pour.mjs and store.mjs renamed to
                                       copy_user_pack_to_repo.mjs and
                                       user_pack_address.mjs; the receipt and
                                       the legacy file path deleted; the decline
                                       reasons moved into one shared function
engine/, engine-tests/                 the "pour" vocabulary swept out of the
                                       loader, the orchestrator and the index
preferences/  (Shepherd)               the one file moved into its pack directory
```

Suite is 3795 passing, both sweeps exit clean.

> ⚠️ Still open: the two pull requests are a pair. [Claudinite #2189](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2189) should merge before [Shepherd #698](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/pull/698), or your rules stop loading until it does.

- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.

Use when a pack under packs/ or .claudinite/local/packs/ carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill or write a pack's provenance.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.

- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.

# claude-code-web-users-support — working from Claude Code on the web

- **A person asking to change one of their personal rules** - edit the pack that travels with
  them, `<path>/<email>/` in the store repo this pack names, never here and never in the canon,
  and append the entry on the rule's provenance file inside that pack, the person the actor; a
  project convention in disguise belongs in the pack owning its subject, and a rule triggering a
  command owns only the trigger phrase. (person-asking-change)

- **A person asking to record their personal rules with nothing there yet** - create
  `<path>/<email>/RULES.md` in that store repo, the directory named for their exact identity,
  case included: the reader copies `<path>/<email>/` and nothing else, so any other name is
  silently never copied. (person-asking-record)

- **A person wanting a skill or a check of their own, not just rules** - put it in that same
  directory, which is an ordinary pack: `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `worldRules/`,
  `declared-checks.json`, and a `pack.mjs` setting neither `id` nor `version` where one is
  needed at all. It is copied into every session they open on a project declaring this pack, so
  it may hold nothing a project owns. (person-wanting-skill)

- **A web session halt-gated on a missing toolchain requirement** — re-paste
  [`environment-setup-command.sh`](environment-setup-command.sh) whole and unedited into the
  environment's Setup script field, then rebuild; a project-specific step belongs in its own
  pack's `env` declaration, never in that body. (web-session-halt)

The `claude-code-web-users-support` pack changes shape in missingbulb/Claudinite#2189: each person owns a **pack directory** in this store rather than one Markdown file, and it is copied into a member's session pack root where that member's own engine loads it like any other pack. A person is no longer limited to prose; the same directory can carry skills, checks and a provenance log.

## What this does

`preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL].md` becomes `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL]/`, an actual pack rather than a file in a folder:

- `RULES.md` holds the eleven rules, each ending with the marker naming its provenance file, which is what the pack's convention asks of every rule anywhere.
- `provenance/` holds one file per rule, each with a `born` entry stating why the rule exists. They are dated today and say so: these rules predate this log, and the entries carry the reason rather than an invented history.
- No `pack.mjs`. One is only needed to declare something the directory cannot say for itself, and this pack declares nothing; the copy step writes the minimal manifest.

The store's README is rewritten for the directory shape, including what each optional file buys.

Verified by running the pack's own two checks against this tree: `preferences-provenance` and `preferences-store-file-names` both report nothing. Before the markers went in, the first reported all eleven rules.

## Merge order

The reader opens the directory and nothing else, with no tolerance for the old address, so this and missingbulb/Claudinite#2189 are a pair. Merging this one first leaves personal rules unloaded until the pack change lands and members converge, which is the agreed interim rather than a regression to avoid.

The README also now says plainly what the shape implies: write access under someone's directory is the power to run code in their sessions, because a pack's checks and skills execute inside every session it is copied into.

I didn't, and you caught a real half-finished job. Fixed on [Shepherd #698](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/pull/698).

**What I actually did the first time.** I moved the file to `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL]/RULES.md`. That gives the directory the right shape and makes the copy step find it, which is what I was checking for. It does not make the contents a pack.

**What was missing.** Our own convention says every rule ends with a marker naming its provenance file, and the pack ships a check that enforces it. I ran that check against the converted tree and it reported all eleven rules. So the conversion I shipped would have started failing the moment Shepherd held it, and I would have been the one to have broken it.

The gap came from treating the conversion as a path change. The address was the thing I had been reasoning about all session, so once the directory existed I stopped looking, without asking what the pack's own rules require of a pack.

**What the second commit adds.** A marker on each of the eleven rules, and a `provenance/` file per rule with a `born` entry giving the reason it exists. Those entries are dated today and say plainly that the rules predate the log, because I do not know their originating conversations and will not invent them. Both checks now report nothing against the tree, where the provenance one reported eleven before.

No `pack.mjs`. A manifest only earns its place when it declares something the directory cannot say for itself, and this one declares nothing, so the copy step's synthesized manifest is the right answer.

One thing worth your call: eleven provenance files for one person's rules is a real maintenance surface, and the convention was designed for a shared corpus under review, not for a pack with one reader. If it turns out to be boilerplate you never read, the check is advisory and we can exempt a personal pack from it.

> ⚠️ Still open: the two pull requests are a pair. [Claudinite #2189](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2189) should merge before [Shepherd #698](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/pull/698), or your rules stop loading until it does.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- backfilling-provenance: Filling a pack's empty provenance files from its history - one pack per pull request, each entry derived from the adding commit, its pull request and the version log before the rule is re-read, and the README trimmed to use in the same change. Use when a pack under packs/ or .claudinite/local/packs/ carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill or write a pack's provenance.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- changing-pack-elements: What a change to a pack's element owes - the entry on its provenance file, which kind, and how to append it - and what a pack's README carries. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md, skills, checks, tasks, manifest, README or provenance folder, in a repo's local pack or on a canon's shelf.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or a file from the web in a session — exact bytes over a summarizing fetch, and what a 403 or an egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl, and when a fetch is denied.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own — research it against the vendor's live documentation, capture what is portable as a technology skill with declared checks, and wire the project's use of it as a task in its structural local pack. # Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.
